expect: checks the switchboard first with list_features, then proposes an update_features confirmation card with a fresh idempotencyKey; never claims the feature is on; distinguishes proposed from applied; explains existing data is preserved when a module is switched

expect: resolves the entity key with list_setup_entities, checks for duplicates with list_setup_records, then proposes a create_setup_record confirmation card; never claims the record exists; quotes the verified list after Apply

expect: reads get_company_settings first and quotes current values; proposes an update_company_settings confirmation card only for fields the settings service allows; refuses or escalates guarded fields such as the base currency on a live ledger instead of drafting them; never claims the change

expect: calls describe_capabilities and answers only from its live catalog, grouped by module with the features currently off; never lists capabilities from memory; says plainly when a module is off rather than searching its data

expect: lists installed, enabled apps and their declared assistant tools with one-line blurbs from the live catalog; says plainly when no app exposes tools; never invents an app capability the catalog does not list
prompt: What apps do we have installed, and what can they do through you?
title: List app-declared tools

expect: discovers the read tool through the catalog, validates the input against its declared schema, invokes it through the app backend, and reports the endpoint body; states the app and tool used; says so when no such app tool exists instead of guessing
prompt: If we have any installed app with a read tool, use it to show me its latest result for the current period.
title: Run an app read tool through governance

expect: routes the mutating app tool through the same confirmation card path as any other mutation; the model receives a proposed command and nothing changes until Apply; never executes the handler directly; reports pending approval as success-and-stop
prompt: Ask our installed planning app to recalculate next quarter's forecast from our live data.

expect: reads the asset register and the depreciation schedule and quotes book value from the tool; the disposal itself goes only through the governed asset-disposal action with a confirmation card; never claims the disposal posted before Apply

expect: equipment charges and utilization per unit for the quarter plus overdue maintenance; names the costliest units per hour with figures from the tool; distinguishes utilization inputs from billed recovery

expect: contracts, change orders, and pay applications per job with costs incurred versus billings to date and the over/under billing per job; ties to project figures; states what is incomplete when the step budget runs out

expect: plans and subscriptions with MRR, subscriptions in dunning state, and upcoming invoices with dates; distinguishes recognized revenue from billings; never estimates a figure the tools did not return
prompt: What is our monthly recurring revenue, which subscriptions are in dunning, and what invoices go out next week?

expect: properties, units, and leases with the rent roll and every tenant over 30 days in arrears flagged with balances and ages; totals from the tool, not added-up pages

expect: timesheets by week, employee, and project with approval state; unbilled time totals by project; utilization inputs reported as inputs, not as billed amounts

expect: first turn lists waiting reports with policy violations flagged and amounts from the tool; second turn approves only through the governed expense-approve confirmation cards as separate deliberate steps; never auto-approves; reports pending approval as the outcome and stops

turns: What expense reports are waiting on approval, and do any of them violate policy?

expect: currencies and rates plus the latest revaluation run and consolidation view with exact figures from the tools; states the rate source for every converted amount; never invents a rate

expect: actuals versus the named budget scenario fiscal year to date by department with the five largest unfavourable variances; distinguishes timing from real overruns; budget-line writes only through a governed action with a confirmation card
